Detect potential cross-contamination between samples

Source: R/contamination.R
detectCrossContamination.Rd

Identifies iSNV sites where a high-frequency variant in one sample appears at suspiciously low frequency in another sample from the same sequencing run, consistent with index hopping or sample cross-contamination.

Usage

detectCrossContamination(
  whe,
  runCol = NULL,
  sourceMinFreq = 0.2,
  sinkMaxFreq = 0.05,
  sinkMinFreq = 0.005,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with multiple samples.

runCol

Character scalar (optional). Column name in colData identifying the sequencing run/batch. If NULL, all samples are compared against each other. A name that is not a column of colData is an error. Samples whose run is NA are left out of every comparison, with a warning giving their number.

sourceMinFreq

Numeric scalar. Minimum frequency in the "source" sample for a variant to be considered a potential contaminant origin (default: 0.20).

sinkMaxFreq

Numeric scalar. Maximum frequency in the "sink" sample for a variant to be flagged as potential contamination (default: 0.05).

sinkMinFreq

Numeric scalar. Minimum frequency in the "sink" sample (default: 0.005). Variants below this are likely noise, not contamination.

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default for source), only consider QC-passed variants in the source sample. A source call that flagISNV failed for being above its maxFreq (0.5 by default) is still used when it has the read depth, alternative reads and strand balance that every filter in qcFilters(whe) asks for: a high frequency is the signature looked for, and the frequency ceiling is there for the iSNV analyses. Other QC steps do not record why a call failed, so a call above maxFreq that one of them also flagged is used too.

Value

A DataFrame with columns:

source_sample

Sample where the variant is at high frequency.

sink_sample

Sample where the variant appears at suspiciously low frequency.

chrom

Chromosome/segment.

position

Genomic position.

ref

Reference allele.

alt

Alternative allele.

source_freq

Frequency in the source sample.

sink_freq

Frequency in the sink sample.

freq_ratio

sink_freq / source_freq – lower values are more suspicious.

run

Sequencing run (if runCol provided).

Details

Index hopping occurs when adapters are exchanged between library molecules during pooled sequencing, causing reads from one sample to be misassigned to another. The signature: a variant at high frequency (e.g., 80%) in sample A appears at very low frequency (e.g., 0.5-2%) in sample B sequenced on the same flow cell, at a ratio consistent with the expected hopping rate (typically 0.1-2% for Illumina platforms).

This function does not require external metadata beyond what is in colData. For finer control, use the output DataFrame to implement study-specific contamination criteria.

References

Bendall EE et al. (2022). SARS-CoV-2 genomic diversity in households highlights the challenges of sequence-based transmission inference. mSphere 7:e00400-22. doi:10.1128/msphere.00400-22

Costello M et al. (2018). Characterization and remediation of sample index swaps by non-redundant dual indexing on massively parallel sequencing platforms. BMC Genomics 19:332. doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200, 300), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "C", "G")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("T", "G", "A")
## Sample A has pos 100 at 80%; sample B has same pos at 1%
freq <- matrix(c(0.80, 0.05, 0.30,   # sample A
                 0.01, 0.40, 0.00),   # sample B
               nrow = 3, ncol = 2)
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = freq),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("A", "B"),
        run = c("run1", "run1")))
detectCrossContamination(whe, runCol = "run")
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 10 columns
#>   source_sample sink_sample       chrom  position         ref         alt
#>     <character> <character> <character> <integer> <character> <character>
#> 1             A           B         seg       100           A           T
#> 2             B           A         seg       200           C           G
#>   source_freq sink_freq freq_ratio         run
#>     <numeric> <numeric>  <numeric> <character>
#> 1         0.8      0.01     0.0125        run1
#> 2         0.4      0.05     0.1250        run1
